name: Rhabdomyosarcoma of the cervix uteri

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Cervical Rhabdomyosarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant small round blue cells with rhabdomyoblastic differentiation on histology
Positive immunostaining for desmin, myogenin, and MyoD1 confirming skeletal muscle lineage
MRI or CT showing a cervical mass with local invasion but no distant metastasis at diagnosis
Detection of PAX3-FOXO1 or PAX7-FOXO1 fusion genes (rare in embryonal subtype but may be tested)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of rhabdomyoblastic differentiation with positive immunohistochemical markers (desmin, myogenin) is required; imaging and molecular studies support diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing is more relevant for alveolar subtype; embryonal subtype is most common in cervix.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Exophytic cervical mass with grape-like appearance
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic gross morphology in many cases
searchTerms: exophytic neck growth with clustered appearance
vaginal bleeding not related to period

common.symptomName: Urinary frequency or urgency due to mass effect
searchTerms: frequent or urgent urination from mass
urinary symptoms due to pelvic growth

common.symptomName: Palpable cervical mass on pelvic examination

occasional.notes: Due to tumor bulk or associated lymphadenopathy

searchTerms: difficulty passing stool due to pelvic growth
tiredness due to low blood count

rare.symptomName: Lower extremity edema due to lymphatic obstruction
searchTerms: lower limb edema due to lymphatic obstruction

rare.symptomName: Metastatic symptoms such as bone pain
searchTerms: pain in bones due to metastasis
symptoms from cancer spread to bones

laboratory: Anemia due to chronic blood loss
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous cervical mass with possible local invasion
CT scan for staging and detection of metastases
genetic: Rare detection of PAX3-FOXO1 or PAX7-FOXO1 fusion genes in alveolar subtype
No consistent genetic marker for embryonal subtype
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for desmin, myogenin, MyoD1

distinguishingFeatures: Negative for muscle markers on immunohistochemistry
Negative or variable muscle marker expression
Clinical presentation and imaging localize tumor site
